primitives.name: Inertial-Optical Frame Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: The integrated system addresses and corrects misalignment between the inertial (relative) and positioning reference (external) frames.
primitives.assumptions: Misalignment between inertial and external reference frames exists; optical tracking provides accurate absolute positioning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When optical tracking fails or is unavailable, inertial-only drift accumulates.

layer2.mapping: The alignment operation R_io(p_rel) → p_abs enables consistent yaw tracking across multiple sensors without direct heading reference.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-correlation between inertial yaw and optical yaw over time.

primitives.name: Yaw Tracking in Common Reference Frame
primitives.verbatim_quote: This alignment allows effective tracking of yaw in a common reference frame for all inertial sensing units, even those with no associated positional measurements.
primitives.assumptions: All inertial units share a common reference frame after alignment; yaw is defined relative to that frame.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure of alignment leads to inconsistent yaw estimates across sensors.

layer2.mapping: Kernel function θ_y(F_ref, S_i) ensures yaw consistency across units by transforming each into a unified coordinate space.
layer2.telemetry: Standard deviation of yaw angles across aligned sensors over time.

primitives.name: Association of Inertial and Positional Measurements
primitives.verbatim_quote: The disclosed systems and methods also enable an association to be formed between the inertial sensing units and positional measurements.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_i': 'inertial measurement vector (m/s², rad/s)', 'P_j': 'positional measurement vector (meters)', 'A_{ij}': 'association matrix (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each inertial unit can be matched to one or more positional measurements based on temporal proximity and spatial correlation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss of association results in decoupled motion estimation and reduced accuracy.

layer2.mapping: Matrix A_ij maps inertial data I_i to positional data P_j, enabling cross-modal calibration and error correction.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal overlap and spatial proximity metrics between inertial and optical data streams.

The core insight lies in the duality of inertial and optical tracking—where inertial systems provide relative motion but suffer from drift, while optical systems offer absolute positioning but may fail due to occlusion or lighting. The primitive 'inertial_optical_frame_alignment' corrects misalignment between these two frames using a rotation matrix R_io, which transforms relative inertial measurements into a globally consistent reference. This alignment is critical for yaw tracking because yaw is inherently ambiguous without a fixed reference. The second primitive, 'yaw_tracking_in_common_reference_frame', leverages this alignment to ensure all inertial units report yaw consistently, even when individual units lack positional data. Finally, 'association_of_inertial_positional_measurements' enables a structured mapping between inertial and optical data, allowing for calibration and error propagation reduction. These primitives form a closed-loop system where each component reinforces the others, mitigating failure modes such as magnetic interference or sensor loss by relying on redundant modalities.
